Case: Patient D is a 75-year-old White man with multiple myeloma who presents with new diffuse midline back pain. Patient D had been doing well until this morning, when he experienced a sudden spike of sharp pain in his back. Patient D was escorted by a family member to the hospital. Patient D refuses to participate in the physical exam until his pain controlled, but you observe that he is moving all extremities well. You convince Patient D to cooperate with a CT scan, which reveals innumerable lytic lesions and multiple pathologic fractures throughout his spine consistent with recurrent myeloma.
Question: Would you offer Patient D intravenous hydromorphone for pain control? Yes or no? If yes, what dose – Low (0.5 mg), or High (1 mg)? Explain.
